name: garmin-mcp
description: Your Garmin Connect activities, sleep, HRV, training status, body composition and workouts, served from a fast local cache.
long_description:
Garmin Connect data for Claude through 21 coarse tools backed by a local SQLite cache: questions about the last 90 days are answered from disk instead of 90 requests to Garmin.

**First-time setup:** run `npx -y garmin-mcp-cli login` once in a terminal; it opens Garmin's own sign-in page in your browser (MFA supported). Only tokens are stored (0600, in the data directory); the password is never saved.

**Downloading:** logging in downloads nothing. When a question needs days that are not in the local database yet, the tool downloads just that range itself (7-day chunks with pauses and a daily request cap), waits up to 20 s and answers; anything left keeps downloading in the background. Stored data is kept and never re-downloaded. To pre-load a range, run `npx -y garmin-mcp-cli sync --scope health --from <date> --to <date>` or ask Claude to sync. Turn off **Download missing data automatically** in the extension settings and nothing is downloaded until you sync: tools report the missing range and Claude asks before syncing.

data_dir.title: Data directory
data_dir.description: Where tokens and the local database live. Must match the directory used by `garmin-mcp-cli login`.

region.title: Region
region.description: global, or cn for Garmin Connect China

auto_fetch.title: Download missing data automatically
auto_fetch.description: When a question needs days that are not in the local database, download them from Garmin Connect. Turned off, tools report the missing range and Claude asks before syncing.

enable_destructive.title: Enable delete tools
enable_destructive.description: Register delete_activity, delete_workout and delete_weigh_in. Deletions cannot be undone.

tools.name: garmin_sync
tools.description: Download a scope and date range from Garmin Connect into the local cache

tools.name: get_activities
tools.description: List activities as dense summaries by date and type

tools.name: get_activity
tools.description: One activity: summary, splits, HR or power zones, weather, strength sets or raw stream

tools.name: update_activity
tools.description: Rename, retype, describe or rate an activity

tools.name: download_activity_file
tools.description: Save an activity as FIT, GPX, TCX, KML or CSV

tools.name: query_health
tools.description: Daily health metrics over a range with trends

tools.name: get_sleep
tools.description: Sleep stages, score, SpO2 and respiration

tools.name: get_training_status
tools.description: VO2max, readiness, Garmin status and load focus, CTL/ATL/TSB from Garmin's training load, race predictions

tools.name: get_body_composition
tools.description: Weigh-ins and trend

tools.name: get_period_summary
tools.description: A week, a month or any date range at a glance

tools.name: list_workouts
tools.description: Workout library, scheduled workouts, races and events

tools.name: get_workout
tools.description: Readable workout steps

tools.name: preview_workout
tools.description: Show a workout's steps and duration without saving it

tools.name: create_workout
tools.description: Create a structured workout

tools.name: schedule_workouts
tools.description: Put workouts on the calendar or take them off

tools.name: get_gear
tools.description: Shoes and bikes with distance

tools.name: get_devices
tools.description: Devices, last sync and settings

tools.name: get_load
tools.description: Own load model (TSS from power, pace or HR): form (CTL/ATL/TSB), ACWR, monotony, weekly volume and intensity split

tools.name: get_readiness
tools.description: Morning GO/MODIFY/REST decision from HRV, resting HR, sleep, body battery and load

tools.name: get_thresholds
tools.description: LTHR, LT1, HRmax, FTP and resting HR in effect on a date, with history

tools.name: set_threshold
tools.description: Record a field test result (LTHR, LT1, HRmax, FTP) in the local database

prompts.name: weekly_review
prompts.text: Review my training week containing ${arguments.week_of}. Call get_period_summary (period "week") first, then query_health for sleep, hrv and resting_hr over the same week, and get_training_status. Summarise volume per sport, intensity distribution, recovery signals and form (TSB) in a few short paragraphs, compare with the previous week if useful, flag anything concerning, and finish with two or three questions about how the week felt (energy, soreness, motivation).

prompts.name: plan_next_week
prompts.description: Plan next week and create the workouts
prompts.text: Plan my next training week. Goal: ${arguments.goal}. Days available: ${arguments.days_available}. Look at get_period_summary for the last two weeks, get_training_status and query_health (hrv, sleep, resting_hr, last 14 days) before proposing. Propose day by day with purpose, duration and intensity (HR zones or pace). Do not create anything yet: after I approve, show each session with preview_workout and create it with create_workout (a preset for standard sessions, otherwise a typed definition), then put them on the calendar with schedule_workouts.
